blocks.text: The Sharing Files Externally workflow can be broken down as follows:

blocks.item: Admin Configuration:
On the Share Files Externally page, the admin can:
Choose to allow specific domains, any domain, or none.
Select which users, groups, or departments are authorized to share files externally.
Activate the policy to enable the feature for the designated endpoints.
To learn more, see About Endpoint Data Scan Sensitive Information: Share Files Externally and Configuring Share File Externally Settings.
User Execution on the Endpoint:
An authorized user right-clicks the desired file on their endpoint, and selects Zscaler > Share File Externally. The Secure File for External Sharing window appears.
In the Secure File for External Sharing window, the user can add up to 10 email recipients and clicks Protect File.
See image.
Recipients must belong to the authorized domains configured in the Share Files Externally Settings page.
The system encrypts the file locally and converts it into a secure HTML format; the file is not transported by Zscaler during this step.
The user then shares the secure HTML file using any preferred method, such as email, Slack, instant message, or removable storage.
External Recipient Access:
Upon opening the encrypted HTML file, the recipient is notified that the content is protected by Zscaler.
To view the content, the recipient must download the Zscaler Secure File Viewer tool for their specific operating system.
See image.
Using the tool, the recipient browses the encrypted file within the viewer and enters their email address.
The system verifies the email’s authorization and sends a One-Time Password (OTP) to the recipient’s inbox.
The recipient enters the OTP into the viewer and clicks Unlock File.
The file is then decrypted and ready for use by the external recipient.
Admin Visibility and Control:
In the Share Files Externally page, the admin can:
View a comprehensive list of all shared files.
Review the file owner, recipient list, and file sensitivity details (including DLP engines and AI/ML categories).
Monitor all decryption attempts and successful access events.
Revoke access to any file at any time by deleting it from the list or editing the authorized recipient list.
